items.prompt: Render the argument of this song in a Gen-Z voice: direct, a little feral, zero cringe, no slang overload. Keep every doctrinal claim intact — voice changes, content does not. No new doctrines, no comparisons, no meta-commentary, no quoted terms. ESSENCE: [0] Mind-wind dissolved in the inward aim; seeing yet not seeing with steady gaze — this is śāmbhavī mudrā by the guru's grace alone: reality free of void and non-void.

paragraphs.text: Eyes open, pupils frozen, mind melted inward: seeing and unseeing at once. That is the whole practice, and it is not a technique you do.
It only lands as grace. Your teacher gives it, and what it opens is reality past both void and non-void. No forcing it. Ever.

ESSENCE: [0] Each sacred form defined by a vanishing: mantra where letters unnoticed, mudrā where all bodily action dissolved, yoga where breath-flow exhausted — then the festival: for the wise attaining Your abode, everything wonderful.

paragraphs.text: Mantra is what remains when letters drop out. Mudra is what remains when effort drops out. Yoga is what remains when breath drops out. Each holy thing is defined by its vanishing.
Then the punchline: for those who get there, everything is wonderful. All of it. That is the celebration.
